correctness.rationale: For a designated r-subset of sinks in one bipartition, forced incident edges leave B_{a−r,b} acyclic orientations; mixed-part sink sets are impossible. Subset marking gives A_{a,b}(z)=B_{a,b}+∑_{r≥1}C(a,r)B_{a−r,b}(z−1)^r+∑_{r≥1}C(b,r)B_{a,b−r}(z−1)^r, hence bivariate EGF B(x,y)[exp((z−1)x)+exp((z−1)y)−1]. With H=1−(exp x−1)(exp y−1), diagonal p_n=2c_n(z)/c_n(1)−1, c_n(z)=[x^ny^n]exp(zx+y)/H. At ρ=log2, H_x=H_y=H_xx=H_yy=−2, H_xy=−4, and independently computed Q=16ρ³(1−ρ)>0. Khera–Lundberg's source theorem verifies strictly minimal diagonal smooth point; applying entire-numerator ACSV uniformly on bounded |z|≤R gives c_n(z)/c_n(1)=exp((z−1)ρ)+O_R(n−1). Then p_n(z)=2^z−1+O_R(n−1), Cauchy estimates give all-k error C_R/(nR^k) and summable TV error. Independent exhaustive orientation counts for n=1..3 gave sink histograms 2; (12,2); (186,42,2) agreeing with poly-Bernoulli totals 2,14,230. Symbolic Q identity proved independently. Finite tests do not establish ACSV bounds.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The limiting PGF 2^z−1 follows after marking all sink subsets and applying the known ACSV machinery uniformly in a bounded complex marking parameter. Existing longest-path and total-count results do not imply the all-k sink law without this new marked construction; the finite unique-sink theorem gives only one atom. The derivation is an application of known general methods, so novelty credit is restricted to the quantitative specialized law.

value.rationale: Natural intrinsic count of terminal vertices in uniformly random acyclic bicliques has a nondegenerate, non-Gaussian, fully specified limiting distribution with a quantitative total-variation rate and geometric uniform local controls. A useful benchmark contrasting with the known Gaussian longest-path statistic; not merely another isolated finite table or a restatement of the unique-sink atom.

final_claim: For a uniform acyclic orientation of labeled K_{n,n}, the sink-count probability generating function p_n(z) satisfies sup_{|z|≤R}|p_n(z)−(2^z−1)|=O_R(n^{−1}) for each fixed R>1. Thus sinks converge in total variation to zero-truncated Poisson(log 2), with local errors ≤C_R/(nR^k), mean 2 log 2 and variance 2 log 2(1−log 2) up to O(n^{-1}).
limitations: Source tree could not be independently enumerated using available GitHub connector; necessary source blobs were fetched at assigned frozen commit, with result and verifier SHA recorded.
Full older sink-polynomial manuscripts were not read cover-to-cover; only specifically stated passages and available full HTML mathematical sections are grounds for comparisons.
Parameter-uniform ACSV correction is justified by analytic compactness reasoning beyond the source's stated uniformity in coefficient directions; no explicit numerical error constants are provided.
No claim for unbalanced bicliques, sharp leading TV constant, or other graph families.
